aliases: Decoupled Clip and Dynamic sAmpling Policy Optimization
definition: A GRPO variant that drops the KL penalty and adds clip-higher, dynamic sampling, token-level policy-gradient loss and overlong reward shaping. It appears in this archive in three roles. As a recipe it is the baseline entropy interventions modify, in one case changing only which tokens receive gradient and nothing else. As a dataset, DAPO-Math-17K is what several sources train on, usually holding out a split for validation. As an object of analysis it now has an explanation: clipped tokens are reported to have low probability, so relaxing the upper bound for positive samples preserves exactly the updates that raise entropy — which is why clip-higher works — while a separate study finds clipping thresholds to be one of three factors governing entropy dynamics alongside off-policy update count and data diversity. Its reported gains are also among those that largely do not survive symbolic variation of the benchmark problems.

evidence.note: Shows that the roughly 20% of CoT tokens with the highest entropy act as decision forks, and that restricting RLVR policy-gradient updates to only those tokens matches or beats full-gradient training, with the advantage growing with model size.
evidence.title: Beyond the 80/20 Rule: High-Entropy Minority Tokens Drive Effective Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning

evidence.note: Reduces the question of whether an update raises or lowers entropy to the sign of one scalar per token, shows that under GRPO what matters is that scalar's deviation from a policy-weighted baseline rather than its own value, and proves the deviation averages to zero over a batch.
evidence.title: On the Entropy Dynamics in Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

evidence.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
evidence.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

evidence.note: A systematic empirical study of entropy in RLVR that finds entropy correlates with response diversity but only weakly and inconsistently with accuracy, identifies clipping thresholds, off-policy updates and data diversity as its drivers, and argues positive-advantage tokens are what collapses it.
evidence.title: Revisiting Entropy in Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Converts AMC23 and AIME24/25 into symbolic templates whose constants are replaced by sampled variables, requires a model to solve several instantiations of each problem, and finds RL-finetuned models lose most of their reported accuracy under that consistency requirement.
evidence.title: VAR-MATH: Probing True Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs via Symbolic Multi-Instance Benchmarks

evidence.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

name: DAPO
